To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the composite states of superheavy systems stay for a very short time before fissioning.
the formation of super-heavy systems can be studied with CoMD.
the composite states stay for very long times before decaying and that the fission time is of the same order of magnitude as the time of the formation of these composite states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the formation and the evolution of super-heavy systems in heavy-ion collisions.
the formation of a heavy composite system in a nuclear reaction, its lifetime and decay.
the formation, stability and decay of super heavy systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of the super-heavy systems is not only possible but also that the decay is not a fast process.
the formation of the heavy system is a very slow process, while the decay is a fast process.
the formation and decay of super heavy systems can be understood in terms of the dynamics of a few nucleons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can observe a new kind of fission process, the so-called “delayed fission”.

the fission process of a heavy system is not a sudden event, but a long lasting process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation and decay of heavy composite systems are strongly correlated and can be described by the same model.
the formation of super-heavy systems can be studied by using the CoMD approach.
